sentences.text: The full moon of 24 November is the largest of the year: the Moon turns full within hours of the point in its orbit closest to Earth.
The Moon's orbit is not a circle but an ellipse; its distance varies between three hundred fifty-six thousand and four hundred six thousand kilometres.
A full moon near perigee looks fourteen percent larger and thirty percent brighter than one at apogee.
In North American tradition the November full moon is called the Beaver Moon: the time when beavers build their lodges for winter.
Now let us look from Earth: the Sun directly behind us, the fully lit Moon ahead.
